title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not part of the cycles/Hodge/Tate material. It is p.115 of a typescript draft of the dimension theory of EGA (the material that became EGA IV_2 §5.5–5.6), annotated by Grothendieck by hand, probably around 1970–71.

The top lines finish a proof. Every finitely generated subalgebra of C[T], and hence of C_r[T], satisfies the chain condition (catenarity).

Corollary 1 is the 'dimension formula'. Setup:
- Y is irreducible and locally noetherian, X is irreducible, and f: X→Y is dominant of finite type.
- ξ and η are the generic points of X and Y, and e = trdeg_{k(η)} k(ξ) is the dimension of the generic fibre.
- For x in X with y = f(x), (13) states: dim O_{Y,y} + e ≥ trdeg_{k(y)} k(x) + dim O_{X,x}.
- Equality holds when O_y is a quotient of a regular local ring.

Proof: the question is local. Take X = Spec B and Y = Spec A with B an integral A-algebra of finite type and A ⊂ B, since f is dominant. Then O_y ⊂ O_x, and (13) is the local inequality (12) (Cohen/Nagata-type) applied to O_y ⊂ O_x.

Remark: trdeg_{k(y)} k(x) = dim( f^{-1}(y) ∩ closure{x} ).

Corollary 2: if x is closed in its fibre and O_y is a quotient of a regular ring, then codim_X closure{x} = e + codim_Y closure{y}. This is (14).

The handwritten additions do three things:
1. They reformulate (13) as a 'hybrid' formula mixing a local-ring dimension with geometric data: dim O_x ≤ dim O_y + dim(O_x ⊗ k(y)) − δ(x), where δ(x) = dim_x f^{-1}f(x) − e, possibly also for non-integral (reduced) schemes ('et réduits').
2. They note that the equality case should be phrased via the '2e condition des chaînes' of Ratliff, that is, universally catenary / quasi-unmixed.
3. Fragmentary notes concern a closed subscheme of X and verifying dimension.

The variant is equivalent to (13). For a fibre F of finite type over k(y) we have dim O_{F,x} + trdeg_{k(y)} k(x) = dim_x F. Hence dim(O_x ⊗ k(y)) − δ(x) = e − trdeg_{k(y)} k(x).
errors: No mathematical error in the typed text. The hypothesis 'quotient of a regular local ring' for equality is correct but stronger than necessary; the published version (EGA IV 5.6.5) uses 'universally catenary', which is what the Ratliff marginal points toward.
In the inline handwritten variant the term should read dim O_x ⊗ k(y), not ⊗ k(x). The left-margin version has k(y) correctly.

ideas.what: Dimension formula / dimension inequality for a dominant finite-type morphism, with equality when the base is universally catenary
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nagata, Grothendieck (EGA IV), Ratliff for the converse

ideas.what: Corollary: codim of a closed point of a fibre equals e + codim of its image
ideas.modern_name: Codimension additivity for universally catenary bases

ideas.what: Hybrid form dim O_x ≤ dim O_y + dim O_x⊗k(y) − (dim_x f^{-1}f(x) − e)
ideas.modern_name: Refinement of the inequality dim O_x ≤ dim O_y + dim O_x⊗k(y) (EGA IV 6.1.2) via the dimension formula
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard; equivalent to the dimension formula

ideas.what: Marginal reference to Ratliff's second chain condition for the equality case
ideas.modern_name: Ratliff: dimension formula holds iff the ring is universally catenary (quasi-unmixed)
ideas.where_published: Ratliff, Amer. J. Math. papers c.1970

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft page of EGA IV dimension theory whose content is published (EGA IV 5.6.5). The handwritten 'hybrid' variant is equivalent to the published formula. The only mildly interesting historical detail is Grothendieck noting Ratliff's chain condition, which dates the annotations to around 1970–71.
transcription_corrections: Inline handwritten variant: 'dim O_x ⊗ k(x)' should be read (and is mathematically) 'dim O_x ⊗ k(y)'; the left margin has k(y).
Marginal '2e cond. des ch. Ratl' = '2e condition des chaînes (Ratliff)'.
The page is a typescript of EGA dimension theory (typed p.115), not cycles/Hodge material; archive page number 103.
